text: A Priestess or Templar of Myrmidia has every right to ride good estalian, arabyan or even bretonnian steeds into battle.
The troops are led to amazing feats of bravery by the mere confidence of being guided by Myrmidia and one of Her skillful warriors.
In a flash of polished armour and shiny robes, the Templar strikes fast and deadly.
Warrior Priests of Myrmidia are master tacticians known in the whole Old World.
The Templar's armour, naturally shiny, turns into an unsustainable beacon of light for the Forces of Destruction.
A stance of mind and shield, and the enemy's onslaught is halted.
A sure thrust in the foulest beast's heart can stop its meaningless flailing.
Charged with the Goddess' holy flame, the Templar's spear strikes the hardest when the arm is strong and the heart is pure. That's what she says, anyway.
Oh, no, not another marathon at dawn.
The Duellist is loyal to the teachings of the father of fencing, focused on balance.
If Figuera is the father of fencing, Estevan is the bastard son. This Duellist uses the off-hand as a lightning-quick defensive tool.

If Figuera is the father of fencing, Casanova is the impertinent grandchild. Like the adventurous teacher, the Duellist focuses on agility of foot and bedazzling assaults that put an end to the fight as soon as possible.
It's good to have someone watching your back against foes looking for a cheap kill. Especially if they know everything about it.
You shoulda seen him, he was-a like a capitone! Kinda greasy, too.
Duellists are usually more comfortable fighting on solid ground rather than on a snorting beast, but they are also adaptable people at heart.
Charge and fire with all weapons! They won't expect that.
Where there is a loaded pistol, there is hope.
A long mission outside the city requires to be locked and loaded. For Orcs.
It is poor form to duel someone without first introducing yourself. Of course, it's a good chance to make the opponent angry and clumsy.
The Duellist explains in detail, more or less politely and technically, how they'll win. More or less.
The Duellist takes pause to analyse and criticise the opponent's fighting technique. The verbal assault is occasionally polite but always substantial.
With a last and complex flourish, the Duellist has a last word on the duel. The opponent likely wishes they were dead at this point.
A parrying dagger won't protect you from darts, but a strike will never hurt you if you know your trigonometry.
A surgical strike at the enemy's sword-hand, and the duel ends before it has even begun.
What do you mean 'You killed my father, prepare to die'? How can you say that when there are about thirty-six pretenders to that role, by today's count! In guardia!
The best Duellists tend to draw the attention of colleagues who'd love to challenge and learn from them, in a non-specific order.
Not all of the really great duellists can dream of becoming a full-pledged Knight Encarmine, but certainly all the Knights Encarmine are great duellists.
